text:
Ottawa trailed 2-0 after 13 minutes and still won, and the numbers say the comeback was earned. The Senators piled up 65 shot attempts to Nashville's 47 and finished with 2.82 expected goals to 2.06, which works out to a 69 percent chance of winning if every shot were replayed. The Predators got their two early goals on a snap shot from Ross Colton (a 20 percent chance) and a power-play wrist shot from Jonathan Marchessault (9 percent), the kind of finishing that rarely holds up for 65 minutes.

The second period is where the game turned. Ottawa generated 1.16 expected goals to Nashville's 0.12, and Tim Stützle cut the lead to 2-1 with a power-play wrist shot at 9:29. Nashville answered with its best stretch in the third, outchancing Ottawa 1.02 to 0.82, and Matt Murray held on, stopping 18 of 20 and beating his expected goals against (2.82) by 0.82. Drake Batherson finally broke through at 18:37 of the third, deflecting in a pass to tie it 2-2. Even strength was oddly tight, with Nashville ahead 1.51 to 1.44, so Ottawa's edge leaned on the second period and its power-play looks.

In the shootout, Batherson was stopped and Ryan O'Reilly scored for Nashville. Then Stützle, who played 26:06 and was named first star, tied it with a wrist shot, and Shane Pinto beat Murray to put Ottawa ahead. Filip Forsberg and Steven Stamkos were both turned aside, and the Senators took the extra point, 3-2.
